title: Define TTFS/TTFP metrics (calculation, exclusions, cohorts) and validation vs billing/usage
creator: Nikhil Sharma
project: Guided onboarding + first production launch checklist
description:
Why
We need unambiguous, consistent definitions for "time to first success" (TTFS) and "time to first production traffic" (TTFP) so (a) Console checklist impact is measurable, (b) funnel and cohort dashboards don’t change week-to-week due to definition drift, and (c) we can validate telemetry against billing/usage sources.

Scope
- Exact metric definitions (start/end timestamps, event sources)
- Exclusion criteria + data quality rules
- Cohort logic (who is included, time windows)
- Validation plan vs billing/usage tables and known dashboard lag
- Backfill approach for pre-launch comparisons (approximation is OK but must be labeled)

Non-goals
- Designing the KPI dashboard UI (tracked in ENG-5815 + dashboard spec)
- Changing event schema (tracked separately; this ticket consumes schema v1)

Definitions (proposed)

1) Tenant/account identity
- Primary unit of analysis: tenant_id (a.k.a. "organization" in Console).
- If a user creates multiple tenants, each tenant is measured independently.
- For workspaces created via sales-assisted provisioning / enterprise imports, we treat them as "non-self-serve" and exclude from default TTFS/TTFP unless explicitly filtered in dashboards.

2) Start timestamp (t0)
TTFS and TTFP both start at the same t0:
- t0 = tenant_created_at (control-plane source of truth).
Rationale: stable, not dependent on Console visits; aligns with "signup" intent. Using first_console_login would bias toward users who visit Console but not API.

3) TTFS (Time to First Success)
Goal: measure the time from signup to the first successful Hosted API call that indicates basic integration is working.

TTFS end timestamp (t_success):
- t_success = timestamp of earliest "hosted_api.request_succeeded" onboarding event for the tenant.

Success event requirements (must all be true):
- Emitted server-side (gateway/control plane instrumentation; not client-only).
- HTTP status is 2xx.
- Endpoint is one of: chat.completions, responses, completions, embeddings, rerank (include OpenAI-compat endpoints that map to these).
- Auth method: API key (exclude internal service tokens).
- Not an internal Redwood tenant (see exclusions).

TTFS value:
- TTFS_seconds = max(0, t_success - t0)
- TTFS is undefined/null if no qualifying success occurs within the observation window.

Observation window:
- Primary reporting: TTFS within 7 days of t0 (TTFS_7d). Users without a success by day 7 are counted as "not activated" for TTFS funnel.
- Secondary reporting: TTFS within 30 days (TTFS_30d) to capture slower enterprise trials.

Edge cases:
- Multiple successes: use earliest.
- Out-of-order events: use event_time (server timestamp) after idempotency/ordering fixes in ENG-5866/PR-28510; for pre-fix data, apply "earliest >= t0" guard.
- If t_success < t0 due to clock skew or late-arriving tenant record: clamp to 0 and flag in data quality (see below).

4) TTFP (Time to First Production Traffic)
Goal: measure time from signup to first meaningful production usage (not just quickstart smoke test).

We will define TTFP in two layers:
A) Primary definition (instrumented, post-launch)
- t_prod = timestamp of earliest "hosted_api.production_traffic_detected" event for tenant.
- Event should be emitted server-side once the tenant meets production criteria (see criteria below).

Production criteria (MVP heuristic; must be documented and consistent):
A tenant is considered to have reached production traffic when ALL are true within a rolling 24-hour window:
1) At least 3 distinct active hours with >= 20 requests/hour (to avoid single burst or one-off load test).
2) Total tokens generated/embedded >= 100k tokens (or equivalent embedding units) in that 24h window.
3) Requests are not solely from known quickstart user agents (e.g., redwood-quickstarts/*) AND not exclusively from Console "Try it" interactions (if applicable).

Notes:
- Thresholds are intentionally conservative; they should correlate with "real usage" while keeping false positives manageable.
- This definition avoids relying on a customer-provided "prod" header that many won’t set initially.

TTFP value:
- TTFP_seconds = max(0, t_prod - t0)
- Primary reporting: TTFP within 30 days (TTFP_30d).

B) Secondary definition (proxy / pre-launch backfill)
For tenants created before the production event exists (or if event coverage is incomplete), we compute t_prod_proxy as the first timestamp where production criteria are met using usage logs + billing tables.
- This MUST be labeled "TTFP (proxy)" in dashboards and analyses.

5) Exclusions (default dashboard view)
Exclude tenants from default TTFS/TTFP reporting if any of the following is true:
- Internal Redwood tenants (email domain allowlist; internal tenant flag in control plane).
- Synthetic/test tenants created by QA automation (tenant tag "e2e" or known test harness user-agent).
- Tenants created via sales-assisted provisioning / migrations (source = "sales_provisioned"), unless the dashboard filter includes them.
- Fraud/spam tenants (risk flag from Trust/Safety pipeline, if available) — pending confirmation from Security/Compliance that this flag can be used for analytics.

Include by default:
- Self-serve Hosted API tenants (standard signup flow).

6) Cohort logic
Default cohorts for reporting:
- By signup week: cohort = ISO week of tenant_created_at (e.g., 2025-W09).
- By region: tenant_home_region (from control plane).
- By acquisition channel (if available): e.g., console_signup, marketplace, partner.
- By SDK family: inferred from user-agent tags (python, typescript, go, openai-compat, unknown).

Cohort inclusion rules:
- Tenant must have t0 within the selected date range.
- TTFS/TTFP computed relative to that t0 (do not shift cohorts based on first event time).

7) Data quality and safeguards
We will implement the following checks in the analytics dataset jobs:
- Missing tenant_created_at: drop row and count as "invalid_tenant_record".
- Negative durations (t_success < t0 or t_prod < t0): clamp to 0; count separately.
- Event duplication: dedupe on (tenant_id, event_name, idempotency_key) when available; else dedupe on (tenant_id, event_name, request_id).
- Late-arriving events: allow updates up to 72 hours; after that, freeze cohort metrics (but keep a "late_event_count" monitor).
- Freshness SLA for onboarding datasets: < 2 hours lag for event-driven TTFS; < 6 hours lag for usage/billing-derived proxy metrics.

8) Validation plan (telemetry vs billing/usage)
Validation goals:
- Confirm TTFS event coverage and alignment with first billable usage.
- Confirm TTFP heuristic matches customer reality (reduce false positives from load tests).

Validation steps:
1) TTFS reconciliation (weekly for first month post-launch)
- For a sample of tenants (n=200 across cohorts), compare:
  a) t_success (event) vs
  b) first_billable_request_time (from usage/billing)
- Expectation: difference <= 5 minutes for P95 (event should be near-real-time).
- If drift > 5 minutes or systematic lag appears, open Telemetry pipeline issue and annotate dashboard.

2) Funnel count reconciliation (daily automated)
- Compare count of tenants with >=1 success event in last 24h vs count of tenants with >=1 billable request in last 24h.
- Alert if absolute delta > 3% for 2 consecutive days.

3) TTFP spot-check with Support/CS
- Select 20 tenants that meet TTFP criteria; have Support confirm via CRM notes / customer comms whether they actually went live.
- Document false positives and adjust thresholds if needed.

4) Known issue: usage dashboard lag
- We should treat usage dashboard UI latency as separate from metric computation latency. TTFS/TTFP datasets must use raw usage/billing sources, not the Console aggregated view.

9) Deliverables / outputs
- Written spec (this ticket) that is linked from:
  - onboarding KPI dashboard spec
  - PRD metrics section
  - telemetry ADR
- A "metric contract" summary (1 pager) for Support/PM/Exec readouts:
  - exact definitions + what changes would be considered a breaking change
- A validation checklist for dashboard go/no-go

10) Open questions (need decision)
- Production thresholds: confirm request/hour and token thresholds with Hosted API PM + SRE (Nikhil + Sean).
- How to tag quickstart traffic reliably across SDKs (user-agent tags are in progress; confirm OpenAI-compat coverage).
- Whether to include embeddings-only tenants in TTFP thresholds (tokens vs embedding units conversion).

Acceptance criteria
- TTFS and TTFP definitions are approved by Hosted API PM (Nikhil), Console PM (Marissa), and Telemetry lead (Logan).
- Cohort and exclusion rules are explicit enough that two people implementing independently produce matching results.
- Validation plan includes at least 2 automated reconciliation checks with alert thresholds.
- Backfill/proxy metric is clearly labeled and does not silently replace primary definition.

References
- ENG-5815: Onboarding KPIs dashboard and alerts
- ENG-5844: Backfill onboarding events / baseline metrics
- Onboarding event schema v1 (Confluence)
- Support top issues Q1 2025 (for interpreting false starts vs real activation)
comments: 2025-02-12 — Chris Osei: Drafting TTFS as tenant_created_at → first 2xx. Question: should "first success" require streaming success separately? I propose streaming as a checklist step, but TTFS should count non-streaming success to avoid penalizing non-streaming use cases.

2025-02-13 — Logan Wright: +1 server-side event for TTFS. For TTFP, prefer an event emitted by an aggregator job rather than trying to do it in gateway inline. Otherwise hard to do rolling windows + token thresholds without heavy state.

2025-02-14 — Marissa Cole: From Console perspective, we need TTFS_7d and TTFP_30d available as cohort filters + overall P50/P75. Also need a clear definition of "excluded" tenants so we don’t get questions about internal dogfood skewing charts.

2025-02-18 — Sean Gallagher: Token threshold is fine but please set it high enough to avoid classifying load tests as prod. Also add data freshness alerting; onboarding funnel charts going stale will page us anyway.

2025-02-24 — Mei Lin: For reconciliation: billing table has request_start_time in UTC with ~5–15 min ETL. If we expect <=5 min diff, we should compare to raw gateway logs dataset, not billing ETL, for the strictest check.

2025-03-04 — Nikhil Sharma: Approved TTFS definition. For TTFP, I’m OK with heuristic thresholds for MVP but want an explicit "TTFP (proxy)" label. Also: include embeddings-only tenants by converting to equivalent token units (need mapping from Metering).
2025-03-12 — Chris Osei: Marking as In Review pending final sign-off from Telemetry on the reconciliation thresholds and which source is canonical for first_billable_request_time.
